### cavity3dBenchmark

This example measures the performance of $\OpenLB$ on a three-dimensional lid-driven cavity. It is based on the setup of [[`laminar/cavity3d`](/examples/laminar/cavity3d/cavity3d.qmd)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}[`laminar/cavity3d` (@sec-example-laminar-cavity3d)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}.
It runs a fixed number of time steps on a cube of $N^3$ cells and reports the throughput in million lattice updates per second (MLUPs), which makes it the reference case for comparing platforms, numbers of processes and resolutions.
The flow itself is the setup of `laminar/cavity3d`; it is not run to a steady state and not evaluated.

#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I \subseteq [0,1]^3 \times \R_{\geq 0}$ is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^3$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid with kinematic viscosity $\nu \in \R_{> 0}$ and constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= -\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p + \nu \Delta \vel \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I.
\end{align}

#### Boundary conditions

As in [[`laminar/cavity3d`](/examples/laminar/cavity3d/cavity3d.qmd)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}[`laminar/cavity3d` (@sec-example-laminar-cavity3d)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}, the lid $\Gamma_D$ at $y = L$ (MN 3) moves with $\vel = (u_\text{lid}, 0, 0)^\top$ and the other five walls $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ (MN 2) are at rest, $\vel = \mathbf{0}$ (@fig-cavity3dBenchmark-domain).
The fluid is initially at rest.
For performance, both are treated with bounce-back rules: the walls with `BounceBack` and the lid with `BounceBackVelocity`, which are cheaper than the interpolated boundaries of `cavity3d`.
The defines at the top of `cavity3d.cpp` switch this: without `LID_DRIVEN_BOUNCE_BACK`, local velocity boundaries are used, and without `LID_DRIVEN`, the lid is a resting wall as well.

#### Domain

The fluid fills a cube of side length $L = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ (@fig-cavity3dBenchmark-domain), with $u_\text{lid} = 1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $\nu = 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$, that is $Re = 1000$.

![Domain and boundary conditions of `cavity3dBenchmark`, the same as in `cavity3d`, with the material numbers (MN) assigned in `prepareGeometry()`.](/examples/laminar/cavity3d/doc/fig/cavity3dDomain.svg){width="60%" #fig-cavity3dBenchmark-domain .lightbox}

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid of $N^3$ cells with the lattice spacing $\Delta x = L / N$, where the default is $N = 100$.
The mesh is split into `CUBOIDS_PER_PROCESS` cuboids per process, by default one.

The LBM collision operator is the BGK operator with a single relaxation time ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), used as `BGKdynamics`, together with the D3Q19 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)).
The lattice uses single precision. With the preprocessor macro `FEATURE_FP16` enabled, the populations are stored in half precision.
The descriptor stores the velocity in a field of its own, so that it can be written to the VTK output.

::: {#lst-cavity3dBenchmark-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<NavierStokes,
                    Lattice<float, descriptors::D3Q19<descriptors::VELOCITY>>>;
```
Case definition for the `cavity3dBenchmark` example, without the `FP16` feature.
:::

The unit converter `UnitConverterFromResolutionAndLatticeVelocity` uses the lattice velocity $0.01$, so the time step size is $\Delta t = 0.01\, \Delta x / u_\text{lid}$.
Lattice statistics are switched off, as they cost time in every step.
The parameters are given in @tbl-cavity3dBenchmark-params. The physical values are fixed in `prepareLattice()`.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | $N$ | $100$ | cells per side length $L$ |
| `TIME_STEPS` | | $1\,000$ | number of time steps |
| `reporter/timer/LATTICE_ITER_T` | | $100$ | interval of the timer output in time steps |
| `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` | $L$ | $1\,\mathrm{m}$ | side length of the cavity |
| `VTK_ENABLED` | | `false` | write the VTK output before and after the time loop |
| `CUBOIDS_PER_PROCESS` | | $1$ | number of cuboids per process |
| `PHYS_DELTA_X` | $\Delta x$ | $L / N$ | lattice spacing, derived from the resolution |

: Parameters of `cavity3dBenchmark`, as set in `main()`. {#tbl-cavity3dBenchmark-params}


#### Results

Every $100$ time steps, the timer reports the progress and the current throughput, and at the end the total wall time and the average throughput.
It also appends one line per report to `tmp/profilingData/performance.csv`, with the resolution, the number of time steps, the number of processes and the throughput.

The job script `scaling.job` runs the benchmark on a GPU cluster with the PBS batch system.
It considers the total cell counts $10^9$, $2 \cdot 10^9$ and $3 \cdot 10^9$, each multiplied by every power-of-two node count up to the number of nodes the job got, keeps the resolutions with at least $3 \cdot 10^6$ cells per process, and calls `./cavity3d --RESOLUTION <N> --TIME_STEPS 1000 --VTK_ENABLED 0` with $12$ processes per node for each of them.

#### Files

```
cavity3dBenchmark/
├── cavity3d.cpp   main(): parameters; mesh, geometry, lattice, initial values and time loop with timer
├── scaling.job    PBS job script for scaling runs on a GPU cluster
└── Makefile
```

The timer output goes to the console and to `tmp/profilingData/performance.csv`. With `VTK_ENABLED`, the velocity and the pressure are written to `tmp/vtkData/`.
